learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental principles and main methodologies of machine learning.
Analyze cases of supervised and unsupervised learning.
Design and implement software systems capable of solving the considered problems.
Evaluate the effectiveness of the chosen methodology for solving a given problem.

syllabus_topics: Python - Introduction to the programming language.
Use of Python for data analysis.
Empirical study of the behavior of random variables.
Introduction to Machine Learning (ML) Instances, features, labels, training set, test set, goal, generalization error, empirical risk minimization, overfitting, evaluation. Types of machine learning.
Unsupervised Learning: Clustering - Concept and formalization.
Gaussian mixtures and estimation via Expectation-Maximization (EM).
Clustering case studies and implementation in Python.
Supervised Learning: Classification - Linear models for classification: formal definition, examples; Perceptron algorithm.
Formalization for a finite hypothesis class. Introduction to Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning.
Classification case studies and implementation in Python.
Supervised Learning: Regression - Introduction, linear regression, and polynomial regression.
Regression case studies and implementation in Python.
Evaluation - Validation, validation for model selection (Train-Validation-Test split, k-fold cross-validation)
Statistical significance, Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE), and confidence intervals.
teaching_methods: Use of technological tools (moodle and/or other educational tools, software, videos, quizzes)
Theoretical lectures using both the blackboard and the computer
Asynchronous activities and exercises to be completed on the Moodle platform

assessment_methods.method: Coursework to be completed throughout the course via the Moodle platform

assessment_rules: The evaluation of acquired knowledge and skills will be based on the completeness of acquired knowledge, the ability to solve a learning problem using proposed techniques, the correct use of technical terminology, originality and independence in identifying suitable methodologies, and the ability to interpret results. In the event that the instructor has any doubts regarding the manner in which the written examination was completed, including concerns about the authenticity of the responses, the student may be required to attend an oral examination.
